title: The Influence of Specific Bioactive Collagen Peptides on Body Composition and Muscle Strength in Middle-Aged, Untrained Men: A Randomized Controlled Trial

what_it_measured.text: The main purpose of this RCT study was to investigate the efficacy of the identical specific collagen peptides combined with RT on body composition and muscle strength in middle-aged, untrained men.
Efficacy Outcomes The primary endpoint of this study was to compare differences in fat free mass between the group receiving collagen peptides (CP-G) and the placebo group (P-G).

dose.text: They ingested 15 g of specific collagen peptides (n = 30; CP-G), placebo (n = 31; P-G), or whey protein (n = 36; WP-G) daily.

endpoint.text: Comparing the changes in the maximum voluntary isometric contraction (N) between CP-G and P-G was also considered as secondary endpoint.
Comparing the changes in fat mass, body weight and waist circumference between CP-G and P-G were defined as the secondary endpoints.
Efficacy Outcomes The primary endpoint of this study was to compare differences in fat free mass between the group receiving collagen peptides (CP-G) and the placebo group (P-G).

reported_results.text: The main analysis revealed a statistically significantly higher increase in fat free mass (p = 0.010) and decrease in fat mass (p = 0.023) in the CP-G compared with the P-G.

All participants had significantly (p < 0.01) improved levels in fat free mass (∆CP-G = 3.42 ± 2.54 kg; ∆P-G = 1.83 ± 2.09 kg; ∆WP-G = 2.27 ± 2.56 kg), fat mass (∆ CP-G = −5.28 ± 3.19 kg; ∆P-G = −3.39 ± 3.13 kg; ∆WP-G = −4.08 ± 2.80 kg) and leg strength (∆CP-G = 163 ± 189 N; ∆P-G = 100 ± 154 N; ∆WP-G = 120 ± 233 N).
The decrease in fat mass was also statistically significantly higher (p = 0.023) in CP-G (∆CP-G = −5.28 ± 3.19 kg) compared with P-G (∆P-G = −3.39 ± 3.13 kg).
These results are in line with the changes in the estimated skeletal muscle mass (∆CP-G = 1.23 ± 1.25 kg; ∆P-G = 0.514 ± 1.05 kg; p = 0.011; d = 0.621).
For this parameter, the baseline data were imbalanced with a significantly lower mean waist circumference in the P-G in comparison with the CP-G (p = 0.011).
In the group of participants that had received the specific collagen peptides the effect was slightly higher with a decrease of 3.1%.
